15 peer-reviewed journal articles · 315 citations (as of July 2026) ·
[Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=9LJsXtMAAAAJ&hl=en)

## Areas of work

[Estimand & endpoint strategy]{.pill}[Target trial emulation]{.pill}[Real-world evidence]{.pill}
[Bayesian & adaptive designs]{.pill}[Oncology trials]{.pill}[Inflammation & immunology]{.pill}
[Empirical Bayes]{.pill}[Data privacy]{.pill}

Much of my recent work sits in two places: using **target trial emulation** to
bring observational data to bear on questions trials answer slowly or not at all,
and **endpoint and estimand strategy** — deciding what a trial should measure
before arguing about how to analyse it.
